(2) Elimination of environmental deficiencies impacting the area.
(3) A more efficient plan of land use in the area.
(4) The provision of improved infrastructure facilities.
(5) Negation of the environmental impact of the proposed Downtown Expressway on adjacent residential areas in Randolph.
(6) The significant adverse environmental impacts associated with the project are the following: (1) the environmental disturbance normally associated with construction, such as increased dust, noise, traffic disruption; and (2) Temporary, and in a few cases, permanent, relocation of residents who live in the redevelopment areas during the construction of new residential units; (3) Impact of the Downtown Expressway on the environment of the northern portion of the project, including the effects of traffic noise and air pollution.
5. Alternatives Considered
a. No action
b. Change in the type and size of the project.
c. Relocation of the project to another site.
6. Comments have been requested from the following: 
a. Council on Environmental Quality
b. Office of Economic Opportunity
c. Department of Health, Education, and Welfare
d. Department of Transportation
e. Governor's Council on the Environment
f. Virginia Department of Highways
g. Richmond Regional Planning District Commission
h. Conservation Council of Virginia
